overview.description: Maniglia (also spelled Mariglia) is a four-player partnership trick-taking game from Sardinia, Italy. Known as 'Bridge Sardo' (Sardinian Bridge) for its depth of strategy, it belongs to the Manille family of games. The Seven is the highest and most valuable card of each suit, giving the game its name ('maniglia' means handle or lever).

history.origins: A Sardinian variant of the Manille family of games, most popular in the North of the island, especially around Sassari, Olbia, and Nuoro.
timeline: Traditional: Developed as a regional variant in Northern Sardinia
Present: Known as 'Bridge Sardo' due to its strategic depth and partnership cooperation
Modern: Remains popular in Sardinian social clubs and family gatherings
history.evolution: Shares etymology with Manille, Manillen, Malilla, and other European games where a specific card (often the Seven or Ten) holds special value.
history.cultural: Played in Sardinian cafes and social clubs, known for allowing open communication between partners about their hands.

setup.players: 4 players in two fixed partnerships (North-South vs East-West), partners sitting opposite each other.
setup.deck: 40-card Italian deck of the French-suited Genoese pattern. Ranking: 7 (Maniglia) > Ace > King > Jack > Queen > 6 > 5 > 4 > 3 > 2. Note: Jack ranks higher than Queen.
setup.dealing: Deal passes to the right after each hand. Dealer shuffles, player to left cuts (minimum 5 cards each portion). Deal anticlockwise in packets of 5 cards (two rounds), so each player has 10 cards. The bottom card (dealer's last card) indicates trumps and is placed face up.

rules.objective: Be the first team to reach the target score (commonly 35 or 45 game points).
rules.gameplay: Player to dealer's right leads to first trick. Must follow suit if possible. Must beat opponent's card if able when an opponent is winning the trick.
keyRules: Follow suit if possible. When an opponent is winning the trick, must beat their card if able. When unable to follow suit, must trump unless partner is winning, you have no trumps, or cannot beat an existing trump. Trick winner leads to the next trick. First team to reach the agreed target score (35 or 45 game points) wins the game.

strategy.basic: The Seven (Maniglia) is the most powerful card - 5 points and unbeatable in its suit. Guard your Sevens and Aces carefully. Remember that Jacks outrank Queens.
strategy.intermediate: Create voids (renoang) by discarding your only card of a suit on a trick your partner is winning. This allows you to trump when that suit is led later.
strategy.advanced: Communication strategy: The player with the stronger hand should take control, asking specific questions to guide play while revealing minimal information about their own cards. Coordinate with partner to capture opponent's high cards.
tips: Track which Sevens and Aces have been played - this determines which cards are now highest in each suit
The 10 tricks each contribute 1 bonus point - winning more tricks matters even without high cards
If dealer turns up a 7 of trumps, they immediately score 5 points - this can end the game instantly

list.name: Exposure of cards when dealing
list.description: Dealer may expose the top card of packets dealt to first two players (and last two); if a trump is exposed, further cards from that packet exposed until non-trump or all five seen. Tournament rules forbid exposure.

difficulty.easy: Random play without following suit properly; doesn't communicate effectively
difficulty.medium: Follows suit and trump rules; basic card counting; simple communication
difficulty.hard: Expert communication strategy; perfect card tracking; optimal void creation and trump management

considerations: Trump suit dynamics and void creation timing

additional: Research by Zach Smith with Sardinian players

scoring.description: Card points: each 7 (Maniglia) 5, Ace 4, King 3, Jack 2, Queen 1; 6-2 (frilli) 0. Each trick adds 1 point. Total 70 points per hand. Team with more than 35 card points scores the difference as game points. First team to reach the agreed target (commonly 35 or 45) wins the game.
